findings.title: Blocked-email match statistics are miscounted because a validator writes to the database
findings.description:
`BlockedEmail.should_block?` is a predicate that also increments `match_count` and sets `last_match_at`. It is called from `EmailValidator#validate_each` (`lib/validators/email_validator.rb:13`), so the count depends on how many times validation runs and whether the surrounding transaction commits.

- **Double validation in signup:** `UsersController#create` validates twice per request, at `app/controllers/users_controller.rb:168` (`user.valid?`) and again at `:172` (`user.save`).
- **`:do_nothing` records:** the save succeeds, so both increments commit and one signup counts as 2.
- **`:block` records:** the save fails validation, and as I read ActiveRecord's save semantics that rolls back the increment made inside it. Only the earlier `user.valid?` increment survives, so the count is right by accident.
- **Save-only paths:** `User.create_for_email` (`app/models/user.rb:103`) and `EmailToken.confirm` (`app/models/email_token.rb:53`) call only `save!`, so a blocked match there records nothing.
- **Lost updates:** `record.match_count += 1; record.save` is a non-atomic read-modify-write, and the `save` return value is ignored.

Split the lookup from the stat recording, and record with an atomic `update_all("match_count = match_count + 1, ...")` invoked once from a deliberate place.

findings.title: Blocklist lookup is an exact, case-sensitive match and is trivially bypassed
findings.description:
`BlockedEmail.where(email: email).first` compares the raw string. `User` does not normalise email before validation: `new_from_params` at `app/models/user.rb:87` assigns `params[:email]` as-is, and there is no downcase callback. `BlockedEmail` does not normalise on write either.

A block on `bad@spammers.org` is therefore bypassed by `Bad@Spammers.org`. This is inconsistent with the domain check in the same validator, which is deliberately case-insensitive (`Regexp.new(..., true)`). `Email.downcase` in `lib/email.rb:19` is already used by `Invite` and `change_email`.

Normalise on both sides: downcase in a `before_validation` on `BlockedEmail` and in the lookup, or compare with `lower(email)`.

findings.title: `rejectedEmails` is shared prototype state, never reset, and shows a misleading reason
findings.description:
- **Shared array:** `rejectedEmails: Em.A([])` is defined in the `extend` hash, so one array lives on the prototype and is shared by every instance. It is never cleared when the modal is reopened. Initialise it in `init`, or reset it where the login controller sets up the modal.
- **Too broad a trigger:** line 274 adds the email whenever the server returns any `errors.email`, including uniqueness ("has already been taken") and domain restrictions.
- **Wrong message:** line 72 then shows `user.email.invalid` ("Please enter a valid email address") for a well-formed address. The address also stays locally rejected for the session even if the server-side condition changes.

Consider storing the server's reason alongside the email, or using a dedicated message.

findings.title: New behaviour has gaps in test coverage
findings.description:
- **Validator spec:** it covers only the two stubbed `should_block?` outcomes. Nothing covers the `record.errors[attribute].blank?` short-circuit, i.e. that a domain-restricted email does not also hit `BlockedEmail`.
- **No unstubbed model test:** nothing shows that a `User` with a blocked email is invalid, or how often stats are bumped. Such a test would have exposed the double count.
- **Controller response:** the new `errors` and `values` keys at `app/controllers/users_controller.rb:198-199` are the contract the JS depends on, but `spec/controllers/users_controller_spec.rb` has no assertions on them in `.create`.
- **JS:** there is no test for the `rejectedEmails` behaviour.
- **Nit:** `describe "#should_block?"` at `spec/models/blocked_email_spec.rb:19` describes a class method and should be `.should_block?`.

findings.title: Domain whitelist/blacklist regex is unanchored (carried over unchanged)
findings.description: `Regexp.new("@(#{domains})", true)` has no end anchor. With whitelist `vaynermedia.com`, the address `x@vaynermedia.com.evil.org` passes, and blacklist entries match as prefixes of longer domains. Only `.` is escaped, so other regex metacharacters in the setting are interpreted. This logic was moved verbatim from `User#email_in_restriction_setting?`, so it is not a regression, but the extraction is a good point to add `\z` and `Regexp.escape` per domain.

findings.title: Blocked address on the change-email path fails late with a wrong explanation
findings.description: `UsersController#change_email` (`app/controllers/users_controller.rb:265-286`) only checks uniqueness before sending the authorisation email. A blocked address is rejected later, in `EmailToken.confirm`'s `user.save!`. That `RecordInvalid` is swallowed by a rescue whose comment assumes "email is already taken", and the user sees the generic `change_email.error`. Checking the block or domain rules up front in `change_email` would avoid sending the email at all.

findings.title: Minor style items in the new Ruby files
findings.description:
- `and` is used for boolean logic where `&&` is conventional.
- `lib/validators/email_validator.rb` has no trailing newline.
- `email_in_restriction_setting?` and `BlockedEmail#set_defaults` (`app/models/blocked_email.rb:21`) are public but are internal helpers and should be private.
- `validates_presence_of :username` at `app/models/user.rb:44` now sits next to the new-style `validates :email, ...`.

findings.title: Validator extraction preserves existing domain-restriction behaviour
findings.description: Moving `email_validator` out of `User` into `EmailValidator < ActiveModel::EachValidator` keeps the whitelist-then-blacklist logic and the `if: :email_changed?` guard intact. `config/application.rb:36` already autoloads `lib/validators/`, so `email: true` resolves. The existing cases in `spec/models/user_spec.rb:488-558` still exercise this path through the model.

findings.title: Migration and model defaults are coherent
findings.description: `action_type` is `null: false` with no DB default, and `before_validation :set_defaults` fills it. The unique index on `email` backs the `uniqueness: true` validation. `Enum.new(:block, :do_nothing)` in `lib/enum.rb` gives 1-based values, consistent with how the fabricator and specs use `actions[:block]`.

structured_findings.summary: Blocked-email match statistics are miscounted because a validator writes to the database
Blocklist lookup is an exact, case-sensitive match and is trivially bypassed
`rejectedEmails` is shared prototype state, never reset, and shows a misleading reason
New behaviour has gaps in test coverage
Domain whitelist/blacklist regex is unanchored (carried over unchanged)
Blocked address on the change-email path fails late with a wrong explanation
Minor style items in the new Ruby files
Validator extraction preserves existing domain-restriction behaviour
Migration and model defaults are coherent
